newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel seals off alley in volatile Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israel seals off alley in volatile Hebron.

text.p: Israeli troops and bulldozers have sealed off an alley in the explosive West Bank town of Hebron where Palestinians threw a bomb at soldiers during clashes on Tuesday.

Two Israeli soldiers were injured, one severely, when the home-made bomb landed at their feet as they aimed their guns at outraged Moslems protesting over posters depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig.
Witnesses said bulldozers worked during the night, shovelling bricks to block entrances to the 20-metre (yard) long alley in the Israeli-controlled section of the divided town.

"The army sealed off an alley in Hebron overnight where home-made bombs were thrown recently at soldiers and border policemen, among them the bomb that wounded two soldiers yesterday," an army spokesman said.
Israeli troops wounded at least 35 Palestinians during Tuesday's violence which flared again along a line that divides the city between Israeli and Arab controlled areas in Hebron.
Palestinians planned to stage a one-hour strike in the town beginning at noon (0900 GMT) on Wednesday. Israel Radio said the army had sent in reinforcements.

Israeli police are holding a 25-year-old Jerusalem woman suspected of pasting posters on Hebron storefronts picturing a pig donning an Arab head-dress with the word Mohammad written on it in Arabic and English.
The drawing depicts the pig stomping with one foot on the Moslem holy book, the Koran, while holding a pen in the other. Islam and Judaism regard pigs as unclean and ban the eating of pork.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and other Israeli leaders have repeatedly condemned the posters -- the latest spark to ignite violence in volatile Hebron.

Israeli troops have clashed with Palestinian protesters almost daily since Israel's groundbreaking of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem last March plunged peacemaking with the PLO into crisis.
